data.name: Run Rabbit Run
data.detailed_description:
Are you a big fan of platform games? Can your nerves tolerate a high level of difficulty? If your answer is yes, then get your jumping skills ready for a new Super Meat Boy and Defrag (Quake3Arena) inspired platformer Run Rabbit Run!

Run Rabbit Run is a dangerously addicting and delightfully challenging game about a bunny angry for carrots. The bunny runs and jumps. And guess what? It also dies a lot. Will you manage to leap over increasingly perilous obstacles and keep your bunny in one piece? Skillful control of jumps, velocity and inertia will allow you to succeed.

Features:

• Comic book style pictorial intro story

• Classical platforming elements and fresh jumping mechanics

• Quickfire nature of levels

• Responsive, finely tuned gameplay

• Stylized silhouetted characters and background

• Well-balanced contrast-based art

• Gorgeous soundtrack featuring live instrumentation and a variety of styles and moods

• 2 tricky chapters and additional "secret" levels

• Tons of challenge and a dose of silliness

Each level in the game is carefully structured and revolves around traversing various obstacles, including spike pits and circular saws of all shapes and sizes. That can be a tricky task unless you are skilled enough to have a perfect control over your jumps. You have to make sure to attain the proper velocity for each jump but you should never forget about inertia which is another important factor to consider. There should not be too much or too little inertia, but just enough to land safely on a platform as any brush with a nearby spike or circular saw is a certain death.

There is no wall-jumping in Run Rabbit Run - good news for players who find it annoying! Instead, there is another challenge which is managing inter-jump velocity in order to land on a platform mid-air. This adds another skill level to the game and a fresh jumping mechanic that you are sure to enjoy.

A thrilling gameplay is complemented with stylish and tasteful artwork. Serene pastel-colored background in the game suggests an atmosphere of tranquility that makes an interesting juxtaposition with the blood-spattered circular saws and spike pits. The silhouettes of the bunny and other animals against the images of trees, snow-capped mountains and cityscape look charming and touching. All this, tied together with an incredible soundtrack, delivers a mixture of blood, action, style and drive that should not be missed!

reviews.review:
Awful. Awful, awful awful. Just a truly maliciously designed game.

You clearly have the potential, the ideas, the talent, and the technical know-how needed to make good, fun games, and instead you waste it on something designed to make people frustrated.

One of the advertised features for RRR is the unique velocity and movement mechanics. Sounds like an interesting concept, until you try it out. Acceleration is exponential. The timing to make each jump requires MILLISECOND level precision. That's the difference between getting nowhere near the platform you're trying to reach, and flying right over the top of it all the way to the other side of the level. It's not a rare occurrence either; you're expected to do this multiple times in a row for most levels, right from the get go. There's also a few quirks to this physics system that aren't explained to the player. Did you know that running away from a wall, jumping, and strafing back towards it lets you gain more height than just jumping? I didn't! This extremely crucial mechanic (without which some levels are simply not possible to beat) isn't explained. It's also likely not something you'd figure out on your own except by complete accident, because it makes no sense whatsoever.

RRR is intentionally malicious. The level design is some of the most evil I've seen in any 'difficult platformer'. Sawblades are placed in spots that will specifically slow you down and force you to navigate around them instead of getting to enjoy the fast paced platforming the game supposedly prides itself on. Red Herrings are added in the form of fake, impossible jumps that waste your time as you keep attempting a solution that's never going to work. Dying instantly brings you back to the start of the level, but doesn't reset the level, so you constantly waste time waiting for sawblades and platforms to move back to the correct position. Levels have to be beaten sequentially, so if you get stuck in a hard spot you're just completely fucked. You can't skip it and go to the next level. I'm never going to get to see the other 2/3rds of this game because I can't get past one specific jump.

The level I'm stuck on requires you to do one of those weird logic defying boomerang jumps I described earlier. This takes place halfway through the level, so you need to have cleared everything before it without dying before you're so graciously allowed to attempt the jump. If you fail at the jump there's a chance you'll fall into the sawblades below, forcing a restart. If you succeed, you now need to do the same jump again on an even smaller platform will less room for error. As if that wasn't bad enough, there's a moving sawblade above the platform. Every failed jump either kills you instantly, or forces you to wait until the sawblade moves into a safe spot. Either way, you're fucked because the level has a timer. Or maybe, that's not the right path at all! Maybe I'm supposed to jump on the distant platforms to the left instead of going up. Do I waste another 30-40 attempts testing that path, only to find out it's impossible, or do I keep wasting my attempts on current jump?

The one positive aspect to this game is that it looks really really great, and the stylistic choices here are fantastic. If you'd used this same artstyle on a regular, fair, fast paced platformer, it would've been fine. I would've loved it. Instead you had to go out of your way to make it cruel on purpose.

I recommend that nobody ever buys this game. If you're thinking about buying this game, I'd instead recommend that you take the $5 you would've spent on it and instead use it to buy a set of dice. Try rolling each of them one at a time, and get a 6 on each one. If you roll anything other than a 6, start over and get your friend to punch you in the throat as hard as they can. Scroll through the screenshots on the store page while you do it, so you can have the benefits of the good artstyle and awful gameplay at the same time!
